findings.source_passage: the Tyre of this Carthage;—the place where the first dead American whale was stranded. Where else but from Nantucket did those aboriginal whalemen, the Red-Men, first sally out in canoes
findings.why_it_matters: The elaboration of Nantucket's primacy—the Red-Men in canoes, the sloop laden with cobblestones—is interpretively important as it establishes Nantucket's mythic origin-status for whaling; the draft keeps only the 'Tyre of this Carthage' phrase and drops all the supporting historical/mythic detail.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least the Red-Men canoe sally and the cobblestone sloop anecdote in compressed form; they carry the mythologizing voice that the bare 'Tyre of this Carthage' tag alone cannot.

findings.source_passage: Ha! thought I, ha, as the flying particles almost choked me, are these ashes from that destroyed city, Gomorrah? But 'The Crossed Harpoons,' and 'The Sword-Fish?'—this, then must needs be the sign of 'The Trap.'
findings.why_it_matters: The ash-box / Gomorrah joke and the ironic naming logic ('The Trap') are voice-establishing comic moves; the draft jumps straight to the Black Parliament scene without any of this, erasing the transition and a signature ironic digression.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the ash-box stumble and the Gomorrah quip at minimum; the 'sign of The Trap' punchline should follow to preserve the comic-naming motif.

findings.source_passage: What a pity they didn't stop up the chinks and the crannies though, and thrust in a little lint here and there. But it's too late to make any improvements now.
findings.source_locator: paragraph 8, after 'this body of mine is the house'
findings.why_it_matters: This self-deprecating philosophical extension of the window/body metaphor is a signature voice moment—Melville's characteristic darkly comic deflation; the draft keeps the metaphor's opening but cuts its payoff entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'chinks and crannies' / 'too late to make improvements' lines after the body-as-house observation.

findings.source_passage: Poor Lazarus there, chattering his teeth against the curbstone for his pillow... Euroclydon! says old Dives, in his red silken wrapper—(he had a redder one afterwards) pooh, pooh! What a fine frosty night
findings.why_it_matters: The Lazarus/Dives contrast is a key thematic passage on poverty and privilege that the critical tradition repeatedly engages; the draft skips from the copestone line straight to the Moluccas iceberg paragraph, losing the full ironic exposition of Dives's dismissal and Lazarus's suffering.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Lazarus-chattering-teeth passage and the Dives red-silken-wrapper paragraph; these are not decorative but carry the segment's interpretive weight on class and cold.

findings.source_passage: here and there a candle, like a candle moving about in a tomb
findings.why_it_matters: This simile is a small but distinctively voiced image that sharpens the gothic atmosphere; its omission slightly flattens the prose register at a moment of strong source writing.
findings.suggested_fix: Reinsert 'and here and there a candle, like a candle moving about in a tomb' after 'blocks of blackness, not houses, on either hand'.

summary: The draft loses the Nantucket mythic-origin elaboration, the ash-box/Gomorrah comic transition, the body-as-house payoff lines, and the full Lazarus/Dives poverty-contrast passage—four medium-severity failures that together constitute significant voice erasure and interpretive thinning.
